story: On a sunny Saturday morning at 76 degrees, Gary is at his workbench in his garage, carefully splicing the wiring harness for his golf cart's sound system and light controller. Across the way, Donna is at her kitchen table checking the club calendar for court conflicts before her 10 AM game with Gary, while Hal sits in his own kitchen tidying up his violation notebook, including his notes on the flamingo count and Gary's cart modifications. Meanwhile, Rosa, content with her coffee, looks over her per-diem shift schedule to see what the week ahead holds.
events: Gary (gary workbench): Lay out and splice the wiring harness for the cart's sound system and light controller
Donna (donna club calendar): Check the calendar for court reservation conflicts and club commitments before our 10 AM game with Gary
Hal (hal violation notebook): Review and tidy my notes on the flamingo count and Gary's cart modifications before filing
Rosa (rosa shift schedule): Look over the upcoming per-diem shifts and see what the week looks like

gary.thought_process: It's 7:17 AM Saturday, I'm home, and nobody's around. The memories say I'm supposed to be at the courts at ten sharp to play with Donna, and the cart wiring isn't done. The sound system is the one piece I can safely work on right now, since quiet hours end at 7 AM and L-03 doesn't apply anymore. Lights and anything visible from the street need Architectural Review approval first, and I owe Hal a proper filing, so I'll keep the exterior stuff off the cart until that clears. Interior wiring and the sound system are fair game. The workbench is the place to start: sort out the wiring harness for the speakers and light controller so the hardware is ready once approval comes through. Gets me useful and busy before the ten o'clock game.

parameters.content: Lay out and splice the wiring harness for the cart's sound system and light controller

donna.thought_process: It's 7:17 AM on a Saturday and I'm home. Gary and I agreed to the 10 AM practice game, and the court is booked for a max of 2 hours under L-05. The pickleball bag and calendar are right here. Best use of this hour is making sure I'm ready: check the club calendar for court reservation conflicts and my other club commitments, so nothing steals our slot or the ladder spot.

parameters.content: Check the calendar for court reservation conflicts and club commitments before our 10 AM game with Gary

hal.thought_process: It's Saturday morning, I'm home, and nobody's around. Last night's dinner at Rosa's went fine, so I'm not feeling combative. My goal is still the flamingo count and Gary's cart wiring, and I want the record to speak for itself. The violation notebook is right here. Best use of this quiet hour is to review and update my written entries so the committee filing is accurate and fair, not driven by temper.

parameters.content: Review and tidy my notes on the flamingo count and Gary's cart modifications before filing

rosa.thought_process: It's a new morning and the house is quiet. Last night's dinner with Gary, Hal and Donna went well, and that was my big goal. Now I'm oddly unsure about my schedule: I've been double-checking Friday's shifts all week, and I'm semi-retired with per-diem work, so I should look at the shift schedule and see what the next few days hold before I start filling them with more plans. Nobody's around to talk to, so a quiet check of the schedule is the sensible thing to do.

parameters.content: Look over the upcoming per-diem shifts and see what the week looks like

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
